aliases: Ta Xue Lan Fei orchid scented green tea
processing: Sold as an orchid-scented green tea. The exact method is not well documented; scented greens generally rest a finished base with fresh flowers so that the leaf takes up their aroma.
harvest_season: Not documented for this tea. Mengding greens are usually spring teas, with early pickings the most prized.
appearance_dry: No standard description is recorded; expect a small, tender green leaf, as is typical of fine Mengding greens.
appearance_liquor: Typically pale yellow-green and clear, as with fine Mengding greens.
appearance_wet: Typically small, tender green shoots, as with fine Mengding greens.
taste_profile: Sold as orchid-scented, so expect a floral aroma over a soft, sweet green tea. No detailed tasting record for this name exists.

brewing.notes: General advice for scented greens: keep water cool and early steeps short, as the scent comes out first.

vintage_note: Little is documented about how it is sold. Like scented greens in general, it is best bought from the most recent harvest and drunk within about a year, before the aroma fades.
description:
Meng Ding Lan Fei is an orchid-scented green tea sold under the name of Mengding Mountain in Ya'an, one of Sichuan's historic tea places. It is a rare name, appearing mainly in a few specialist retail lists, and little is documented about it.

The alias Ta Xue Lan Fei points to the same orchid-scented idea. Scented teas usually start with a finished green base and take on aroma from fresh flowers, but no method specific to this tea has been recorded.

Expect flowers first and a gentle green tea underneath, and brew it as you would any delicate scented green, cool and short. A real floral note should fade gently over steeps; a loud, unchanging perfume is a reason to doubt a tea of this type.

Ask the seller who makes it and whether real orchid was used. A similar tea, Meng Ding Snow Orchid, was described by an English-language tea writer in 2010 as a new, real-flower style built on a Ganlu-type base. Whether the two are related is not established.
history: Little is documented about this tea: its maker, date of origin and method are all unclear. It should not be read as one of Mengding's old tribute teas. Orchid-scented Mengding greens appear to be a recent development, with one similar tea described in 2010 as newly reaching the market in small quantities.
